utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Madam Registrar, can you call for the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-95-14-A, the Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. The appearances. I have a problem in my earphones. I don't know that is -- unless it is Mr. Hayman calling.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Hayman is attending by phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And Anto --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Sorry. It's impossible. It's impossible to go on, I'm sorry. I have terrible noises in my earphones. Hello. Let me call for the appearances first. For the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, and with me, Your Honour, are the case managers Ms. Susan Grogan and Mr. Kebba Khan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For the appellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For the appellant, Russell Hayman appearing by phone from Los Angeles and my co-counsel Mr. Anto Nobilo appearing by phone from Zagreb, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Okay. May I first ask Mr. Blaskic if he can understand the proceedings. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I understand the proceedings, and I am able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... may I further inquire how you feel, how is your health. Are you feeling better? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, much better than I was before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. So I understand you can follow the proceedings correctly. Well, I do not have to explain the purpose of this Status Conference as we had quite a number of them through these last years. Let me first, then, ask the Defence whether there is any problem concerning the detention of Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for this opportunity. As you know, we filed a request for an independent medical examination some weeks ago, and with the help of this Chamber an examination was arranged. I have not seen the results of that examination. They may have been given to General Blaskic, but I understand follow-up care and treatment is being organised if it hasn't already occurred, and we are grateful for that and for the Chamber's intervention in this regard. If General Blaskic has other concerns or comments on that situation, I would invite the Court to solicit them from him directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Hayman. So may I turn to Mr. Blaskic. Is there any issue concerning your detention or your health you wish to take up today? Perhaps if you had to raise any issue concerning your health, I would suggest that we go into private session, but if that's the case, of course. Mr. Blaskic. THE APPELLANT: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not unable to -- we're not able to hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters are unable to hear the witness when we switch our microphone on. Once our microphone is off, then we can hear the accused. THE APPELLANT: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We're having a technical problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I can't get the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the technician is on his way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Is the problem fixed, Mr. Blaskic? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I can hear you very well and I'm getting the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We still have a technical problem in the English booth. The minute we turn the microphone on to interpret what Mr. Blaskic is saying, we can no longer hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe until the technical problem is resolved if General Blaskic would mind just stating one statement, one sentence at a time and then there can be a translation of that one sentence and instead of General Blaskic proceeding throughout, if he just says one statement and then the translation, we may be able to proceed. If not, I'm not sure we'll be able to proceed with the difficulties with the translators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Farrell, we can try, but ... Mr. Blaskic, can you try to say one short sentence and then stop a moment for the translation. Maybe we work with -- let's give a try. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions regarding the treatment in the Detention Unit. The staff's attitude to me is very professional and they are behaving correctly in every way. I would like to thank you and the Detention Unit and the officials of the Detention Unit for making it possible to have an independent medical examination. I have not completed all the tests yet, but once the tests are completed, then I will be waiting for the results of the tests. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Blaskic. So when we have the results, we'll know how to proceed on that. Can I now turn to the -- to the case. Well, I don't have much to say except that the Appeals Chamber is preparing the judgement. The hearings were already held in this case, so we are on the way to finalise the decision. It will take still some more time to have it, but I cannot now give any exact date for that. Is there any other issue that the parties want to raise at this juncture? Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: On behalf of the Prosecution there isn't, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: The Defence. Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of the appellant I would simply note that we were surprised by filing by the Prosecutor on 24 March seeking to add to the briefing and indeed to the evidence in the case through the filing of a declaration and submission of the other materials. We filed last night an opposition and a request that that filing be stricken in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hayman, I have just received your response, your objection to the filing of the Prosecution, and I haven't read it yet. I was on the way coming to this courtroom when I got it. So we'll see at the Chambers level how to proceed on the Bench on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I just wanted to indicate, Your Honour, that we haven't even the filing yet and I'm not in a position to comment on Mr. Hayman's comments on the record, obviously. I'm sorry he's surprised. It probably would help us if he would just indicate one way or the other what the allegation is and then we can move on, but we'll wait for the opposition and respond -- or file a reply - I'm sorry - to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: May I? Mr. Farrell wants us to take a position on the nature of the Rule 68 disclosures when we've never had any discovery of the Prosecutor's Office of the Prosecutors involved in the other cases, of the investigators involved in this case and other cases, and respectfully, it's not incumbent on us to take a position of whether Rule 68 violations were intentional or not; and if the Court wants to go into that subject matter, we submit we're going to need to have discovery powers with respect to the Prosecutor's Office and we may need to have a hearing so that, for example, the declarant whose declaration was submitted by Mr. Farrell can be subject to cross-examination, as well as other relevant witnesses from the Prosecutor's office. That is our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Hayman. Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I think we'll wait and respond. It's -- the filing, as you're aware, was simply a request to clarify what their position was during the argument. I'm not in agreement with his proposals, but of course we'll simply respond in writing and put any concerns in writing to you when we file our reply at that time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Well, I take note here of this submission and declaration made by the parties. The Appeals Chamber will wait for the reply of the Prosecution to the objection and then we'll take -- we'll consider the motion and make a decision on it. Well, if there is no other matter to take up, I think -- I think there is none. Am I correct, Mr. Farrell?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: There is none, Your Honour. JUDGE POCAR: Thank you. Then we can adjourn. This Status Conference stands adjourned. Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 4.15 p.m.
